q: Old Monk, the cult Indian dark rum, was launched in which year?
r: Old Monk has been made since 1954, and built its following almost entirely by word of mouth.

q: Which spirit is the base of a classic Margarita?
r: Tequila, triple sec and lime. Mezcal makes it a Mezcal Margarita instead.

q: Feni, the fierce local spirit with a GI tag, comes from which Indian state?
r: Goa. Only feni made in Goa may legally use the name.

q: A Mojito is built on which spirit?
r: White rum, muddled with mint, lime and sugar, lengthened with soda.

q: What does IMFL stand for on Indian liquor labels?
o: Indian Ministry of Food and Liquor
r: Indian-Made Foreign Liquor: foreign-style spirits made in India. Foreign, made locally.

q: Which two ingredients join gin in a classic Negroni?
r: Equal parts gin, Campari and sweet vermouth.

q: Shikanji, the roadside cooler, is essentially which drink?
r: Lemon, sugar, black salt and roasted cumin in cold water. Chaas is buttermilk, aam panna is raw mango, jal-jeera is cumin water.

q: Which Indian rum is nicknamed for a religious figure?
r: Old Monk. Hercules, McDowell's and Contessa are all real Indian rums, but only one is a monk.

q: An Espresso Martini contains which of these?
r: Vodka, coffee liqueur, fresh espresso and sugar. Despite the name, no vermouth and no gin.

q: Aam panna, the summer cooler, is made from what?
r: Raw green mango, roasted and blended with cumin and black salt. Ripe mango makes a lassi or panha-style sweet drink, not panna.

q: Which country drinks the most whisky by volume?
r: India, by a wide margin. Roughly one in two bottles of whisky sold worldwide is poured there.

q: 'Neat' means a spirit served how?
o: Straight from the bottle, no ice, no chilling
r: Neat is room temperature and undiluted. 'Up' is chilled and strained; 'on the rocks' is over ice.

q: Which of these is NOT an Indian spirit or drink?
r: Pisco is Peruvian and Chilean. Feni, mahua and arrack are all South Asian.

q: A Piña Colada blends rum with which two?
r: Rum, pineapple juice and coconut cream. It's Puerto Rico's national drink.

q: In Indian bar slang, a 'chota peg' is what?
r: Chota is small, burra is large. The vocabulary marched in with the British army.

q: Which glass is traditionally used for an Old Fashioned?
r: A short, heavy-bottomed rocks glass, built over a large cube.

q: Toddy, the palm-sap drink, gets its English name from which Indian word?
r: From the Hindi tari, the sap of the palm tree. British sailors borrowed it for their hot whisky cure.

q: What is the primary flavour of gin?
r: Juniper, by law. Coriander and angelica are common supporting botanicals, but juniper must lead.

q: Somaek, the Korean bomb shot, mixes soju with what?
r: Soju plus maekju (beer). The name is a mash-up of both words.

q: Which Indian city is known as the country's craft-beer and pub capital?
r: Bengaluru earned it in the draught-beer boom of the 1980s and now has the most microbreweries.

q: A Daiquiri in its classic form is which three things?
r: Just rum, lime juice and sugar, shaken hard. Add mint and soda and you're heading toward a Mojito.

q: Kokum, used in Konkan coolers, is what kind of ingredient?
r: A sour, deep-magenta coastal fruit. It also makes solkadhi with coconut milk.

q: Which of these is a fortified wine?
r: Vermouth is wine fortified with spirit and infused with botanicals. The others are still or sparkling wines.

q: Nashik, in Maharashtra, is India's capital of what?
r: Wine. Vineyards along the Godavari supply most of India's wine.

q: What does 'on the rocks' mean?
r: Poured over ice. Simple as that.

q: Bhang, traditionally drunk at Holi, is stirred into which drink?
r: Thandai, the almond-rose milk. It's sold at government-licensed shops in cities like Varanasi.

q: A Bloody Mary's base spirit is which?
r: Vodka with tomato juice and spices. Made with gin it becomes a Red Snapper.

q: Which Indian state has been dry since 1960?
r: Gujarat, since 1960. Bihar, Mizoram and Nagaland introduced prohibition much later.

q: What is a 'mocktail'?
r: A cocktail without alcohol. Bartenders also call them zero-proof drinks.

q: Amrut, India's first single malt whisky, is distilled in which city?
r: Bengaluru. It launched in Glasgow in 2004 to prove Indian malt could compete.

q: Which of these is the odd one out as a cocktail base?
r: Angostura is bitters, dosed by the dash. The rest are base spirits.

q: Masala chaas is spiced what?
r: Thinned yogurt (buttermilk) with cumin, black salt and mint, drunk after lunch across India.

q: The Mai Tai belongs to which drinking style?
r: Tiki, the Polynesian-themed style invented in 1930s California. Trader Vic and Don the Beachcomber both claimed it.

q: Sula, Grover and Fratelli are Indian producers of what?
r: Wine. All three helped build India's modern wine industry.

q: What does 'ABV' measure?
r: Alcohol by volume, as a percentage. Proof, in the US system, is double the ABV.

q: A Cuba Libre is rum, cola and what?
r: A squeeze of lime is what separates a Cuba Libre from a plain rum and coke.

q: Tongba, drunk through a bamboo straw, is brewed from which grain?
r: Millet, in the Eastern Himalayas, topped up with hot water as the evening goes on.

q: Which cocktail is traditionally served in a copper mug?
r: The Moscow Mule. The Mint Julep uses a silver or pewter cup.

q: Solkadhi, the pink Konkan digestif, combines kokum with what?
r: Coconut milk, poured after fish curries the way other coasts pour digestifs.

q: Which is a rum-based classic?
r: Dark 'n' Stormy is dark rum with ginger beer. Sidecar is brandy, Vesper gin and vodka, Boulevardier whiskey.

q: Sake is produced by which process?
r: Sake is brewed from rice, so it's technically closer to beer. Soju and shochu are the distilled cousins.

q: Which Indian drink is described as 'cumin water'?
r: Jal-jeera: jal is water, jeera is cumin. Sharp, smoky and savoury.

q: The Aperol Spritz is topped with which wine?
r: Prosecco, with soda and Aperol, over lots of ice in a big glass.

q: Which is India's largest-selling category of spirits?
r: Whisky, overwhelmingly. Brandy leads in some southern states, but whisky dominates nationally.

q: Angostura bitters is best known for its oversized what?
r: Its label, famously too big for the bottle. Legend says one brother ordered bottles and the other labels.

q: A 'shot' in most bars is closest to which measure?
r: Roughly 30–60 ml depending on the country. A barspoon is about 5 ml.

q: Which Indian spirit is distilled from cashew or coconut?
r: Feni: cashew feni from the fruit, coconut feni from palm sap. Mahua comes from mahua flowers.

q: The Cosmopolitan is built on which spirit?
r: Citrus vodka, triple sec, cranberry and lime.

q: Mahua liquor is distilled from what part of the plant?
r: The sweet mahua blossoms. Banned as 'country liquor' under colonial rule, it's now being revived as a heritage spirit.

q: Which cocktail family does the Whiskey Sour belong to?
r: Sours: spirit, citrus and sweet. A flip adds a whole egg; a julep is spirit, sugar and mint over crushed ice.

q: What is India's Kasauli distillery famous for?
o: Being among Asia's oldest working distilleries
r: It has been running in the Himalayan foothills since the 1820s, still using Victorian copper stills.
